issuer.name: Transact Payments Malta Limited (programme manager: Wirex UAB)

funding.supported_assets_note: E-money card linked to the user's Wirex fiat or crypto accounts; the issuer terms call it 'an e-money product; it is not a credit, charge or debit card' although Wirex markets it as 'Wirex Debit Mastercard'. Exchange rates 'vary by currency pair and available liquidity'; the associated exchange fees are shown only in the app.

eligibility.usage_note: Issuer terms: applicants must be 18+ and 'resident in the European Economic Area (but not in Cyprus or Liechtenstein)'. The 28 allowed codes are our expansion of 'EEA' (27 EU members + Iceland + Norway); the source gives no country list. UK, Switzerland and non-EEA countries are served by other Wirex entities/terms and are not covered by this variant. The consumer landing page wirexapp.com/personal now redirects to wirex.one ('Wirex One'), whose supported-country list was not read.

kyc.thresholds_note: No threshold-based tiers: the card 'can be used only once KYC is completed successfully' (issuer terms clause 3.5). Proof of source of funds may be requested at any time.
kyc.stages_note: Account creation with email + phone (SMS); identity verification starts when upgrading to 'Starter' level: government photo ID, selfie/liveness 'depending on your country of residence', proof of address 'may be requested'. Card Terms accepted at card order; a minimum balance may be required to order (amount shown in app). Typically completed within 5 minutes per help centre.

access.note: Free plan for all Wirex users ('Standard Entry'). A 'Standard Enhanced' tier (1% Cryptoback) requires locking 150,000 WXT for 180 days and is modelled as a conditional maximum.

'Standard Enhanced': lock 150,000 WXT for 180 days. No fee for the upgrade beyond the lock.

evidence.title: Wirex Debit Mastercard Terms and Conditions (EEA issuer terms, help centre)
evidence.excerpt: 'Your Card is issued by us' = Transact Payments Malta Limited (MFSA-authorised EMI); Program Manager Wirex UAB (Lithuania). Applicants 18+ and 'resident in the European Economic Area (but not in Cyprus or Liechtenstein)'. E-money product, 'not a credit, charge or debit card'. FX fee 'as set out in the Fees & Limits Schedule'; card usable only after KYC. No effective date.

scope.note: EEA customers only; other regions have separate issuer terms (e.g. 'global' terms naming Wirex Limited / Singapore).

evidence.title: Wirex Fees (help centre fee schedule, by region)
evidence.excerpt: Card issuance free in all regions; ATM free up to EUR 200/month (EEA) then 2%; delivery EEA EUR 5 (DHL World Mail) / EUR 15 (DHL Express); SEPA/Faster Payments/ACH/PIX transfers free; card funding '0% or more' by currency/country; exchange fees 'can be viewed in the app'; GBP 30 administrative fee for ToS violations. No FX fee line, no plan prices, no replacement fee amount, no date.

scope.note: EEA column of a multi-region table

evidence.contradiction_note: FX: schedule lists no FX fee; benefits article claims none; issuer terms allow one 'as set out in the Fees & Limits Schedule'. Modelled as unknown.

evidence.title: X-tras pricing: plans and tiers (help centre)
evidence.excerpt: Standard free; Premium EUR 9.99/month or EUR 102/year; Elite EUR 29.99/month or EUR 306/year, paid in euros. Cryptoback: Standard Entry 0.5% / Enhanced 1% (150k WXT); Premium Entry 1% / Enhanced 2% (250k) / Ultimate 3% (750k); Elite Entry 4% / Enhanced 6% (1.5m) / Ultimate 8% (7.5m); locks of 180 days, no fee for tier upgrades. Table typo '250,00'. No region stated, no date.
evidence.contradiction_note: Read of 2026-10-26 (research list) noted plan payments 'in WXT only'; this read states euro subscriptions. Benefits article states Premium 3% and Elite 'up to 8%' versus Entry rates 1% / 4% here.

evidence.title: Benefits of the Wirex card explained (help centre)
evidence.excerpt: Cryptoback in WXT on all purchases: Elite 'up to 8%', Premium 3%, Standard 0.5%; 'no annual or foreign exchange fees'; 'up to $200 in fee-free withdrawals globally'; virtual card in app, physical card at Visa/Mastercard acceptance points. No issuer, no countries, no date.
evidence.contradiction_note: Premium 3% here vs 1% Entry on the pricing page; '$200' ATM allowance here vs 'EUR 200' (EEA) on the fee schedule; 'no foreign exchange fees' vs issuer terms allowing an FX fee.

evidence.title: Wirex Limits (help centre)
evidence.excerpt: Virtual/Plastic/Metal: max purchase EUR 30k; per month EUR 30k/30k/75k; cash withdrawal per day N/A/EUR 500/EUR 500; per month N/A/EUR 5k/EUR 5k. SEPA up to EUR 50,000 per day. Card top-up min USD 12; unconfirmed card USD 15,000/day, confirmed USD 25,000/day. 'Limits may vary depending on region or currency'; 'all limits are subject to change'. No date.

evidence.title: How to verify your identity (help centre)
evidence.excerpt: Verification starts 'when you elevate your status to Starter': phone number confirmed by SMS, government-issued photo ID, selfie and liveness check 'depending on your country of residence', proof of residential address 'may be requested'. 'Typically, verification is completed within 5 minutes.' No country list, no date.

evidence.title: How to order a Wirex card (help centre)
evidence.excerpt: Physical: 'Get Physical Card', accept Card Terms, top up if prompted, choose delivery option, pay the delivery fee from an account; 'we do not charge any additional fees'; a minimum balance may be required ('exact amount required will be displayed in the app'); delivery several days to four weeks. Virtual: immediate. One physical card at a time. Availability 'varies by region'. No date.

changelog.reason: Initial record from official help-centre pages (EEA issuer terms, fee schedule, X-tras pricing, limits, KYC, card ordering). Single read; second read required before publication. FX fee left unknown (official pages disagree). Product status 'active' from live help-centre order flow and terms, but the consumer landing page now redirects to Wirex One — needs David's review.

Second independent read on 2026-10-30 of all seven evidence pages: every material value is confirmed. Issuer terms (1556): Transact Payments Malta Limited, MFSA-authorised EMI, Program Manager Wirex UAB (Lithuania, 305118023), clause 3.1 '18 or older' and 'resident in the European Economic Area (but not in Cyprus or Liechtenstein)', clause 2.3 e-money product 'not a credit, charge or debit card', clause 15.2 FX fee 'as set out in the Fees & Limits Schedule', clause 3.5 KYC gate, clause 13.5 replacement fee amount not stated. Fee schedule (1379, EEA column): card issuance free, PIN change free, ATM 'Free up to 200 EUR monthly, 2% thereafter', delivery DHL World Mail 5 EUR / DHL Express 15 EUR, SEPA free, card funding '0% or more', exchange fees 'viewed in the app', GBP 30 administrative fee, no FX line, no replacement or inactivity fee, no date. X-tras pricing (1337): Standard free, Premium EUR 9.99/month or EUR 102/year, Elite EUR 29.99/month or EUR 306/year in euros; Cryptoback 0.5/1 (150k WXT), 1/2 (250k)/3 (750k), 4/6 (1.5m)/8 (7.5m), 180-day locks, typo '250,00' still present. Benefits (1301): Elite 'up to 8%', Premium 3%, Standard 0.5% in WXT, 'no annual or foreign exchange fees', 'up to $200 fee-free ATM withdrawals globally' — contradictions unchanged and already modelled conservatively (Premium 1% Entry, EUR 200, FX unknown). Limits (1380): EUR 30k/30k/75k, ATM EUR 500/day and 5k/month, SEPA 50,000 EUR/day, top-up min 12 USD — identical. KYC (1190) and card ordering (1302): wording identical; order flow live (product active). Wirex One post: unchanged, silent on the EEA card. NOT published, two reasons for David: (1) the validator refuses a published tier whose base reward status is 'contradictory' (Premium Entry 1% vs 3% on the benefits article) — policy rule 5 allows publication because the dedicated pricing page is the governing value and the contradiction is displayed, but changing that status is an editorial decision this run may not take; (2) product status: wirexapp.com/personal redirects to wirex.one and no official page states whether the EEA Mastercard continues — the help-centre order flow and EEA issuer terms are still live. No value changed.

editorial.summary: E-money Mastercard issued by Transact Payments Malta for EEA residents (except Cyprus and Liechtenstein), programme-managed by Wirex UAB. Free Standard plan with 0.5% Cryptoback in WXT; Premium (EUR 9.99/month) and Elite (EUR 29.99/month) plans raise the base rate to 1% and 4%, and locking large amounts of WXT for 180 days raises it to 3% / 8%. Card issuance free, ATM free up to EUR 200 per month then 2%. The foreign-exchange fee could not be established from the official pages, which disagree.
good_for: EEA residents who want a free card with a small token-denominated reward
Users already holding WXT who can lock it for higher Cryptoback
not_for: Anyone who needs a documented FX fee before spending abroad (not established)
Residents of Cyprus, Liechtenstein, the UK or Switzerland (other entities/terms, not covered here)
Users who want rewards in fiat: Cryptoback is paid in WXT
watch_outs: Official pages disagree on Cryptoback for Premium (1% vs 3%), on the ATM allowance currency ($200 vs EUR 200) and on whether an FX fee exists; conservative values modelled, FX unknown.
